entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
BIP125 rule 4 specifies that when considering the replacement of a transaction in the mempool, the new transaction must pay not only more total fees than the transactions it replaces but also an additional fee to cover its own bandwidth usage. This ensures that the network is compensated for relaying the larger or new transaction.
The process involves calculating the difference between the modified fees of the new transaction and the conflicting transactions. If this difference, known as nDeltaFees, falls short of the required incremental relay fee for the size of the transaction, the replacement is rejected. The code excerpt demonstrates this logic by checking whether nDeltaFees is less than the incremental relay fee for the given transaction size; if so, it triggers a rejection with an "insufficient fee" error.
Further details on BIP125's replacement rules can be found [here](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0125.mediawiki). This policy maintains the economic integrity of the transaction relay mechanism, discouraging spam and ensuring fair compensation for network resources consumed by higher-priority transactions.
